intro: Rachmaninoff plays the opening of Liszt’s Second Hungarian Rhapsody in his first year of making gramophone records, 1919. This is the first side of Edison Diamond Disc 82169, with the slow Lassan’s shifts between major and minor.

sections.label: A · The piano’s opening call
sections.mNote: A C♯-major chord leads into the minor-key Lassan

sections.label: B · Softer piano phrases
sections.mNote: A quieter continuation after the opening call

sections.label: C · The piano grows forceful
sections.mNote: Stronger phrases emerge from the quieter passage

sections.label: D · The first side continues
sections.mNote: Liszt’s rhapsody continues beyond this disc side

cues.title: C♯ major opens the door
cues.text: Liszt begins on a C♯-major chord, then settles into C♯ minor. The piano seems to speak in the slow Lassan, taking time over its phrases. The fast Friska belongs to the later part of the complete rhapsody.
cues.evidence: The opening major chord, minor-key Lassan and later Friska are described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Rhapsody_No._2. The source identifies this recording as Part I: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Second_Hungarian_Rhapsody.ogg.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Major beside minor
cues.text: Within the Lassan, Liszt turns repeatedly towards C♯ major and E major. The piano’s grave opening has lighter, capricious companions.
cues.evidence: The Lassan’s tonic-major and relative-major passages are described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Rhapsody_No._2, under Form.
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

cues.title: Ten sides for Edison
cues.text: In 1919 Rachmaninoff begins recording for Edison. The contract allows ten released sides, and he plays a Lauter concert grand made in Newark. He asks to approve his performances before release; Edison nevertheless issues different takes of the same pieces.
cues.evidence: Rachmaninoff’s first Edison contract, the Lauter piano and the release of multiple takes are described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Rachmaninoff_recordings. The selected side’s 1919 date and catalogue number are given at https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Second_Hungarian_Rhapsody.ogg.

cues.title: Rachmaninoff meets the Philadelphia sound
cues.text: Rachmaninoff later records his own Second Piano Concerto with Stokowski and the Philadelphia Orchestra, in 1924 and again in 1929.
cues.evidence: The two recordings of Rachmaninoff’s Second Concerto with Stokowski and the Philadelphia Orchestra are documented at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Rachmaninoff_recordings.

composer.born: 22 October 1811, Doborján, Kingdom of Hungary (now Raiding, Austria)
composer.epithet: He could fit an orchestra under ten fingers, then end a lifetime at the piano with a few notes left hanging in the air.
facts: Carl Czerny and Antonio Salieri in Vienna; Anton Reicha in Paris
Free masterclasses; founding president of the Budapest music academy, 1875
Piano works and transcriptions; thirteen symphonic poems; symphonies, concertos and sacred music
composer.background:
Writing from Albano in June 1839, Liszt told Princess Cristina Belgiojoso about the concerts he had been giving alone in Rome. No singer came on between his pieces; no other soloist shared the bill. He played his transcription of the William Tell Overture, fantasies on opera tunes, studies and improvisations. Between numbers he talked to the audience. “The concert is me,” he joked. A single pianist had taken possession of an entire evening.

His father Adam had begun the piano lessons in Doborján, a German-speaking village in the Kingdom of Hungary, where he worked on an Esterházy estate. Hungary remained Liszt’s homeland, though German and French were the languages he used most easily. The family went to Vienna in 1822. Carl Czerny, a former pupil of Beethoven, taught him piano; Antonio Salieri taught him composition. Paris followed in 1823, but its Conservatoire refused to admit a foreigner. Private lessons, including work with Anton Reicha, continued his education.
